title: Streaming `sort` is unstable above the partition threshold without `maintain_order`
verdict: ties keep input order with `maintain_order=True`; without it, not above 32 MiB
description: The streaming sort concatenates its morsels in order and runs the in-memory sort up to `POLARS_SORT_PARTITION_THRESHOLD_BYTES` (32 MiB). Above it, it splits rows into key-range buckets. With `maintain_order=True` each task reads a contiguous run of frames and ties keep input order (Polars's `test_sort_stability_with_duplicate_keys` checks it, also partitioned and spilled). Without it the frames are dealt to the tasks in turn, and ties come out in another order: a sort of 3 000 000 rows on `i % 3` returned the rows of key 1 out of input order (in memory in order).
Below the threshold ties kept input order on every probe, with and without `maintain_order`. Polars documents order among ties only for `maintain_order=True`.
reference: `tie_order`: any order of the ties, and any rows of a tie for a `fetch`. Every behaviour is allowed.

notes: s-sort-ties-large: `sort('k')` without `maintain_order` over 3 000 000 rows; the input indices of key 1 are increasing in memory (True) and not when streaming (False).

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each observation (`STREAMING_OBSERVATIONS`, python/tools/sverify_dev/probe_polars.py) with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')` and records both results. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.
Carried over from polars-sort-stability's round-2 reading, which the probe now confirms for the unordered path.

provenance.notes: Rerun on small inputs (3,000 or 5,000 rows) in a subprocess with POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=64 and POLARS_SORT_PARTITION_THRESHOLD_BYTES=1024, which Polars reads at start-up: the same behaviour as the large inputs at the defaults (the unstable streaming sort, sums and var varying by run), so the probes stay cheap. The variables only move the thresholds; the large-input results at the defaults stand.
